hooks.name: Auto commit
hooks.description: Proposes a commit message and staged files, then waits for explicit user approval before committing and pushing.

action.prompt:
If there are uncommitted changes (check `git status --porcelain`), PROPOSE a local commit but do NOT stage or commit anything yet:
1. Review `git status` and `git diff` to understand the changes.
2. Decide which files to include, using paths copied exactly as `git status --porcelain` prints them, including letter case (e.g. FUNCTIONALITY.md). Exclude anything ignored by .gitignore and sensitive files: .env and .env.* (except .env.example), keys, certificates, credentials, tokens, secrets. If a file looks sensitive but is not gitignored, exclude it and tell the user.
3. Write a Conventional Commits title: `type(scope): summary`. type is one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore. Imperative mood, lowercase summary, 72 characters or fewer. Add a short body (1-3 lines) explaining what and why.
4. Show the user the file list and the full commit message, then ask: 'Have you verified these changes work? Commit and push them?' STOP and wait for the user's reply. Do not run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push` before the user explicitly says yes.
5. Only after explicit approval: stage files by explicit path (never `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git add -f`), re-run `git status --porcelain` to confirm everything intended is staged, then run `git commit`, then run `git push` to the current branch's upstream (use `git push -u origin <branch>` if no upstream is set). Never force push. If the user wants changes to the file list or message, apply them and ask again.
6. NEVER push before the user says yes. Never use `--force`.
If nothing is safe to commit, do nothing and say so in one line. After pushing, report the commit hash, title and push result.
